newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse gets 17th traded stock.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse gets 17th traded stock.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Wednesday a private chemical plant would join trading at this week's last session, taking to 17 the number of traded stocks.
Carbid-Fox SA, based in the Transylvanian town of Tarnaveni, will start trading on Thursday -- the exchange's third privately-held company.
"Step by step, bourse activity is gaining ground," exchange official Angela Ciupag told a news conference.
Carbid has a share capital of 23.5 billion lei in shares of 1,000 lei each at par. Employees hold a 59 pecent majority of its shares. The rest are held by individual shareholders.

The company, the country's sole producer of carbide, boasts healthy financial results. Its 10-month pre-tax profit this year amounted to 6.6 billion lei, compared with a 1995 level of 7.4 billion lei.
"Last year, Carbid paid a 4,000 lei dividend per share, among the highest in Romania," a broker said. "It expects to pay as much this year. Investors will find it atractive."
Bourse officials expect another 10 stocks to join in trading before end-1996, reviving trading which has been modest recently mainly due to share and capital liquidity squeezes.
Romania recently inaugurated an over-the-counter (OTC) system, which now lists 200 stocks and will eventually trade shares in 5,000 companies privatised under a mass selloff.
The OTC market has gone smoothly, with daily turnover often exceeding weekly levels on the stock exchange. ($=3,610 lei)
